implementation: Distribution supplies only two whole unmodified pinned original vendor files, commits, sizes, SHA256 and full notices. A bounded R4U0 tail follows the original R4I total; unchanged original9-module prefix proved byte-identical. Legacy kernels ignore the optional tail. No extra Limine module, Recovery image or installed module entry.

Kernel independently anchors exact origin/catalogue fields and validates both complete vendor formats before any submission. Intel checks main/extended checksums, signature/platform, lengths and loader versions. AMD validates container/equivalence/patch/chipset ranges and Zen full-signature patch identity. Original file SHA is integrity anchor; no invented modern AMD legacy checksum.

Initial profiles: Haswell CPUID306c3/platform mask32/target28; Milan B1 CPUIDA00F11/targetA0011DE and required current baseA0011D9. The older signing-vulnerableA0011D5 fallback and other family19h patches included in the original file are never load approvals.

BSP prepares after its own IDT before CPU/PAT/FPU decisions. Initial AP prepares after its exact GS/IDT before final features/LAPIC/TSC/PAT/FPU. Protected narrow MSR triggers only79 orC0010020 and original CPU admission decides afterward. Runtime logical restart rereads/requalifies, never submits. Virtual CPUs expose virtual revision only and never update.

Whole validated firmware retained in resident4KB-aligned cache before boot memory reclamation. Selected original bytes copied into a separate4KB-aligned owned patch. Nonblocking global claim remains until exact requested revision readback; uncertain submitted loads retain it. Preinstruction Busy returns only its fresh unsubmitted claim and counts0. No borrowed Limine bytes survive restart.

Actual typed Written/Faulted/NotSubmitted outcomes separate instruction attempts from owner refusal. Missing/rejected optional firmware is never submitted and preserves boot-recovery reachability; normal CPU/PAT/FPU qualification continues on BIOS state. Actual uncertain load/readback, changed identity or required runtime reload reject that CPU.

Before/after full finite CPUID capture and exact raw comparison, plus distinct post-baseline capture. Diagnostic fingerprints do not replace common feature/PAT/FPU/module owners. Resident atomic144-byte receipts preserve exact CPU/execution epoch/nonreused publication; foreign/public queries copy only.

Contract35 appends optional R4DEV31 slot82 at672, complete680. All previous672 bytes, records/constants/slots, R4SYS27/1288, DriverApi37 and CPUPOWER184/wire1 unchanged. SDK49 optional Zig/C facade preserves failed outputs and caller tails. Only Spectra38 takes the new SDK pin; CPUPOWER5 and six other module artifacts byte-identical.

Spectra owns METRICS MICROCODE and CHECK SMP/MICROCODE. Raw/decoded CPU/epoch/sequence, revision availability including valid0, hash/provenance and actual trigger attempts remain explicit. Virtual revision/supplied firmware never means physical update success. Existing owned lifecycle verifies full unchanged offline receipt then fresh restart without runtime trigger; original native gates retained.

source_audit.role: Kernel: mandatory initial local update/owned aligned storage/passive atomic receipts only. Distribution: pinned original firmware and backwards-compatible preload appendix. Spectra: userland presentation and explicit checks. No public/runtime load interface.
source_audit.review: Exact whole-file SHA/catalogue/model/platform, Intel checksums and AMD equivalence/patch selection. AMD signed target requires original README base, never vulnerable fallback. BSP after own IDT before CPU/PAT/FPU discovery, AP after own GS/IDT before full admission. Immutable resident cache survives Limine reclamation. Nonblocking aligned patch claim retained through exact revision; uncertain instruction retains it, pre-instruction Busy returns only fresh own claim and counts0. Full raw CPUID equality separate from diagnostic fingerprints; original baseline owners still decide. Optional bad/missing data refused before trigger without blocking durable boot recovery; attempted failures or required runtime reload reject CPU. Exact execution epoch/sequence per CPU, passive copy only; virtual values never physical success. No source owner, stack, FPU, scheduler, GP recovery, timer/idle/power or MCA implementation changes. Existing controlled lifecycle retains complete microcode record offline and obtains fresh restart without runtime update. Actual built27 early/copy/digest/memory bodies no implicit SIMD or direct Runtime/heap/module calls.

source_audit.limits: Physical update success and native Intel/AMD SMT update behavior unqualified. Real local KVM4 pending; synthetic source peers are not hardware proof. disassembly.scope: Actual kernel instruction bodies only; no vendor microcode payload disassembly. Call targets/body checks complement source review, not physical update proof.

source_qualification.host_scopes: Hardware/currentCPU/epoch/admission peers explicit. Actual parser, original payload/SHA, boot control, native cache/claim/staging/store/copy and collector/renderer source exercised; no native host instruction.

runtime.limits: No physical microcode load qualified; all virtual revisions are guest-only, write attempts0. Real local KVM SMP4, natural successful guest poweroff. Retained passive MCA evidence, complete output/header/stale identity and logical offline/restart exercised. Source/synthetic tests cover actual terminal capture algorithms, not real #MC delivery or native AMD error hardware. No current-health, memory-owner or generic correction/persistence claim.

standard.limits: Exactly one final normal Suite3/all4, unchanged workload/reference/method. Boot-only microcode validation and KVM revision receipts do not qualify physical updates, native SMT update behavior or performance gains. Previous32 used a proved lossless transport reexport, preserving original failed export; no method/measurement changes.

review_findings.finding: Exact native source peers prove that a retained uncertain patch prevents a second WRMSR, but bool apply made the second receipt count1 submission. Count only exact Written/Faulted instruction outcomes; pre-instruction Busy/owner refusal counts0 and never releases someone else's held patch.
review_findings.resolution: Typed NotSubmitted/Written/Faulted instruction outcome. Retained uncertain patch prevents a second submission and keeps its owner. Exact protected Busy returns only its fresh unsubmitted claim, with count0. Original failed assertion unchanged; extra direct Busy case added. All hardware operations/currentCPU/epoch/FPU admission peers explicit, no physical update or host CPU probe.

review_findings.reason: Exact optional firmware rejection must not prevent durable boot recovery before filesystem/runtime caches. Never submit invalid data; actual attempted load/readback and runtime required reload remain terminal.
review_findings.resolution: Package rejection is soft before any trigger; uncertain attempted load and runtime reload remain hard. Shared terminal_code owner prevents controller drift. Canonical common feature/PAT/FPU admission unchanged.

review_findings.cause: Tuple Path/Name sort in32 differed from full identity Path/Name OrdinalIgnoreCase. Use full key; every441 original record/field preserved.

limits: Real local KVM SMP4 only. No native-host CPU/MSR/cache probes, remote/OssiPC, real native Intel/AMD update, physical SMT interaction or Windows runtime qualification. Source/synthetic tests and supplied blobs do not prove physical update success.

Only the two exact initial load profiles are admitted; AMD additionally needs the original required base revision. Other supported CPU models still boot on existing firmware under common qualification and expose unsupported/missing/prerequisite status.
Initial early boot only; no runtime microcode interface, arbitrary MSR/blob endpoint, late all-CPU update, userland firmware loading or altered global module baseline.

Boot-only update failures after a real instruction remain hard refusal; protected exception recovery is not rollback of partially updated silicon. Resident patch stays retained when execution is uncertain.
Exactly one final normal Suite3/all4,30 complete4/4 samples and6 valid full unchanged DevCenter readbacks. Fixed workload/reference/method; no isolated speedup or native hardware safety claim.
